title: Weather and the city
theme: Rain changes plans, a metro delay, a long night, the city's moods.

storylets.title: Caught without cover
storylets.note: The first drops, and everyone runs. Common on rainy days.

b1: {A} stops mid-square and looks up as the first drops land.
{A} holds out a palm and finds it wet.
{A} stands by the pond and squints at the sky.
{A} pauses on the stone as the rain thickens.
b2: {A} breaks into a run, bag held over head.
{A} sprints for the awnings, jacket flapping.
{A} dashes across the stones, boots slapping puddles.
{A} runs in a bent crouch, one hand over the hair.
b3: {A} ducks under a shop awning, laughing, and shakes out a sleeve.
{A} reaches a doorway and wrings out a cuff.
{A} arrives under cover and swipes the face with a sleeve.
{A} huddles in the shop doorway, steam rising.

storylets.title: The umbrella goes up
storylets.note: A person with an umbrella. Pure texture.

b1: {A} pops open an umbrella on the step and sets off.
{A} snaps an umbrella up under a dripping awning.
{A} opens a wide umbrella with a flourish.
{A} ducks out of a doorway under a clear umbrella.
b2: {A} walks the length of the block, rain drumming overhead.
{A} crosses the square at a measured pace, heels splashing.
{A} heads along the sidewalk, tilting into the wind.
{A} takes the long way round puddles.

storylets.title: Waiting out the downpour
storylets.note: A person waits under a shop awning for the rain to ease.

b1: {A} stands in a doorway with arms folded and watches the water run.
{A} stays under the awning, heels on the threshold.
{A} lingers in the dry strip by the shop wall.
{A} stands near the glass as the rain hammers.
b2: {A} takes a call, one finger in the other ear.
{A} holds a handset up and says, "It's raining. I'll be late."
{A} talks on the handset for a minute, eyes on the sky.
{A} lifts the handset to the ear and nods.
b3: {A} steps out when the rain thins and heads off.
{A} walks away once the sky lightens.
{A} goes at last, collar up.
{A} leaves the awning at a jog.

log: Phone, one side: {A} says: "Rain's stopping everything. I'll be there in twenty."
Phone, one side: {A} says: "Start without me. Save me a seat."

storylets.title: Delay on the platform
storylets.note: A rainy-day delay, a notice, a call. Stalled people reveal small things.

b1: {A} waits on the platform, one foot on the yellow line.
{A} stands among a dozen others and looks down the dark tunnel.
{A} stays at the platform edge and checks the clock.
{A} waits as the board flickers.
b2: {A} reads the delay board, lips moving.
{A} studies the printed sheet taped to a pillar.
{A} checks the notice board and sighs.
{A} reads the notice twice and rubs the back of the neck.
b3: {A} takes a call and says, "Signal fault. Maybe an hour."
{A} holds the handset to the ear and says, "Start without me."
{A} makes a call and speaks in short bursts.
{A} lifts the handset and mouths a few words.

log: Phone, one side: {A} says: "Train is dead. I'll walk if it's not moving by seven."
Phone, one side: {A} says: "Tell them I'm on the way. Rain's closed the line."

storylets.title: A child and a puddle
storylets.note: Small joy in a wet street.

b1: {A} and {B.desc} come along the sidewalk, {B.desc} two steps ahead.
{B.desc} drags {A} down the block by a sleeve.
{A} and {B.desc} cross the square, rain bouncing off the coat.
b2: {B.desc} plants both boots in the biggest puddle and stays.
{B.desc} stands in the middle of a puddle, arms spread.
{B.desc} stops dead at the curb and stares at the water.
b3: {A} waves a hand at {B.desc}, tries not to smile, and fails.
{A} waves for {B.desc} to come, then gives up and laughs.
{A} waves the umbrella handle and calls something short.

log: Overheard: {A} calls: "Out of the puddle, my {B.rel}! Your socks!"

storylets.title: A bench under a hissing lamp
storylets.note: A long rainy night. Someone sits it out.

b1: {A} sits on a bench with a hood up, rain streaming past.
{A} takes a seat under a hissing lamp.
{A} perches on the bench edge and watches the puddles.
b2: {A} unfolds a small umbrella and holds it low.
{A} spreads a coat and holds it overhead.
{A} lifts an umbrella and rests it on a shoulder.
b3: {A} stands, stretches, and looks up the block.
{A} gets up slowly and shakes out a wet sleeve.
{A} rises and stays at the bench edge, hands in pockets.

storylets.title: A clear sky and a blanket

b1: {A} spreads a blanket on the lawn and weighs the corners with shoes.
{A} flops down on a worn blanket and kicks the shoes off.
{A} lays out a blanket and sets a flask on one corner.
{A} claims a patch of grass with a faded cloth.
b2: {A} eats a flatbread slowly and watches the sky.
{A} drinks from the flask and breaks off a piece of fruit.
{A} eats alone, one knee up, eyes on the towers.
{A} nibbles from a paper bag and leans on one elbow.

storylets.title: Parcel under a coat
storylets.note: A delivery in the rain, carried in under a jacket.

b1: A drone drips onto {A}'s step and drops a parcel.
{A} takes a soaked parcel from a hovering drone.
A courier drone sets a wet crate down and rises.
{A} signs for a dripping package at the door.
b2: {A} hugs the parcel under a jacket and ducks.
{A} tucks the package inside a coat and hunches over it.
{A} lifts the crate in both arms and shields it with a body.
{A} wraps the parcel in a sleeve and holds it tight.
b3: {A} goes in fast and the door slides shut.
{A} enters with rain streaming off the shoulders.
{A} steps inside, dripping.
{A} backs through the door, parcel clutched.

storylets.title: Two strangers, one awning
storylets.note: Rain throws strangers together. One conversation, no follow-up promised.

b1: {A} stands in the shop doorway, jacket dripping.
{A} presses back against the shopfront and watches the water.
{A} waits under the awning with a damp collar.
b2: {B.desc} dashes in beside {A}, bag over the head.
{B.desc} splashes into the doorway and shakes out both sleeves.
{B.desc} bursts under the awning, gasping.
b3: {A} and {B.desc} trade a remark about the weather and then a longer one.
{B.desc} says something that makes {A} laugh out loud.
{A} and {B.desc} chat for a few minutes without moving.

log: Overheard: {B.desc} says: "I'm {B.first}, by the way. Pleasure to be rained on with you."
Overheard: {A} says: "{B.first}? I think I've seen you at the stalls."

storylets.title: The stall packs up early
storylets.note: A keeper closes up in a downpour.

b1: {A} hauls crates under a shaking canopy and stacks them in the dry.
{A} lashes down the awning and carries a pot indoors.
{A} drags a table in with rain on both shoulders.
{A} carries the last tin of broth under a coat.
b2: {A} stands at the empty counter and wrings a rag.
{A} looks at the sky for a long minute, hand on the till.
{A} stays by the stall front, arms crossed, watching the water.
{A} stands under the canopy with the shutter half down.
b3: {A} leaves, the shutter rattling down behind.
{A} comes out of the stall and pulls the cover shut.
{A} leaves with a lamp in one hand and a bag in the other.
{A} locks the shutter and walks off through the rain.
